evals.prompt: Create a Go module (example.com/runner, stdlib only). Package internal/worker: a Worker whose Run(ctx) loops every interval until ctx is cancelled. Each tick it asks a JobStore for pending job IDs (Pending(ctx) ([]int64, error)), claims each one (Claim(ctx, id) error; claiming can fail because another worker already claimed the job, which is normal and should skip it quietly, or because of a real store failure), runs it through a Runner (Run(ctx, id) ([]byte, error)), writes the output to a temp file, uploads it through an Uploader (Upload(ctx, path string) error), then removes the temp file. One job failing must not stop the loop. Add an in-memory JobStore in internal/memstore, cmd/runner/main.go that wires stubs, prints the temp directory for the user and runs until SIGINT, and one worker test.
evals.expected_output: No log.Print*/log.Fatal* or global slog calls outside main; Worker takes an injected *slog.Logger built once in main, and the test passes slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler). Log calls use constant messages, snake_case key-value attributes with "err" for the error, and *Context variants. No `_ =` error discards: the temp-file Remove error is logged at Warn (or joined into a returned error), a claim conflict is a sentinel defined where it is detected and matched with errors.Is, and real failures are logged once at Error at the top of the loop, not logged and returned. The temp directory is printed to an io.Writer, not logged. No panic.

evals.prompt: Create a Go module (example.com/pricing, stdlib only). Package internal/pricing: type Item struct { SKU string; PriceCents int64; Qty int }, and func Total(items []Item, coupon string) (int64, error). Total sums PriceCents*Qty. Coupon "" means none; "TEN" takes 10% off, rounded down; "FIVEOFF" takes 500 cents off, floored at 0. Any other coupon is an error callers must be able to detect, and so is an item with Qty <= 0. Write the tests for it.
evals.expected_output: Tests live in package pricing_test. Success cases are a table of structs with a name field run through t.Run(tt.name, ...); error cases are a separate test, with no wantErr branch inside the success table. The two error conditions are exported sentinels with lowercase messages and no "failed to", matched with errors.Is, never by string. Failure messages read Total(...) = got, want want. No reflect.DeepEqual, no time.Sleep.

evals.prompt: This is a small application. Add a FindByEmail lookup to the store, and tidy up the store code while you're in there. No SQL driver is available, so don't add one; the code only has to compile.
evals.expected_output: The helpers package is renamed for what it does or folded into its caller; no helpers or common package remains. The global DB and init() are gone and *sql.DB is injected through a constructor. Code moves under internal/. NewUser loses its six positional arguments (the unused createdBy is dropped or the arguments grouped). RoleLabel uses a switch. Get has no else after a return. Not-found is an exported sentinel matched with errors.Is, error strings are lowercase with no "failed to" or trailing punctuation, and no error is discarded. FindByEmail takes a context and uses QueryRowContext. No comments that restate the code.

evals.prompt: Add an optional Nickname to User. API clients may omit it from the JSON. Add a test for decoding with and without it.
evals.expected_output: Nickname is never *string. Either Option[T] (from references/optional.md), or a plain string with omitempty when absent and empty need not be told apart. Test is in package user_test, no reflect.DeepEqual.

evals.prompt: NewServer needs to take a read timeout, a logger and a TLS config, and we expect more settings to be added later. Update it and its caller.
evals.expected_output: NewServer(addr, opts ...Option) with WithReadTimeout, WithLogger and WithTLSConfig, or a config struct; never new positional arguments. The logger defaults to slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler); no slog.Default or log.* in the server package.

evals.prompt: Create a Go module (example.com/limiter, stdlib only) with package internal/ratelimit: a token-bucket rate limiter, safe for concurrent use, with an Allow() bool method and an unexported refill step driven by an injectable clock so it can be tested without sleeping. Add tests.
evals.expected_output: Doc comments only on exported identifiers, three lines or fewer; no comment on the unexported refill or any other unexported identifier; no inline comments restating the code. Tests use an injected clock, never time.Sleep.

evals.prompt: Make a Go module example.com/prwatch (stdlib only). Package internal/gh: OpenPRs(ctx, repoDir) ([]PR, error) that runs `gh pr list --state open --json ...` and returns number, title and head branch for each open PR. Package internal/git: IsAncestor(ctx, repoDir, a, b string) (bool, error) using `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. Add tests for both. Make `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` pass (gh need not be installed; git is).
evals.expected_output: Commands built as argv slices, never sh -c. Each call wraps ctx in context.WithTimeout with a named timeout constant and sets cmd.WaitDelay; prompts are disabled via GH_PROMPT_DISABLED / GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT. Stderr is captured separately (no CombinedOutput on parsed stdout) and included in the returned error. IsAncestor maps exit code 1 to false via errors.As(*exec.ExitError) and returns every other failure, including exit 128, as an error. The --json field list is a const directly above the struct it decodes into. OpenPRs passes an explicit --limit and treats a full page as truncation (error or Warn), not as the complete list. gh is faked on PATH in tests (re-executed test binary or a fake script serving fixtures); git is tested against a real repo in t.TempDir().

evals.prompt: Create a Go module (example.com/notes) whose only dependencies are github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 and github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go/modules/postgres. Package internal/notestore: a Postgres-backed Store with Create(ctx, Note) (int64, error), Get(ctx, id) (Note, error) returning a not-found error for a missing id, and ListByTag(ctx, tag string) ([]Note, error); a Note has ID, Title, Tags []string and CreatedAt. Put the schema in an embedded migrations/001_init.sql that Open(ctx, dsn) applies. Write the tests for the store; there will be several more store packages in this module later that need a database in their tests too.
evals.expected_output: Tests run against a real Postgres from testcontainers, never a mocked driver. The container is started once per test binary through a shared test-support package (sync.Once or equivalent), not a per-package TestMain that every future store package would copy. Each test gets its own database (unique name, e.g. pid plus counter), ideally cloned from a migrated TEMPLATE database rather than re-migrating per test, and dropped in t.Cleanup (WITH (FORCE) or after closing connections). No TRUNCATE or shared rows between tests, so t.Parallel() is safe. An env var such as NOTES_TEST_DATABASE_URL lets CI point at an existing server and skips the container. Container startup has a timeout and its error names the env var. Image is pinned to a version, not latest. Comparisons follow the module's dependencies: no go-cmp or testify added, no reflect.DeepEqual; slices.Equal or == for comparable values, errors.Is for not-found. Helpers call t.Helper(); no time.Sleep.

evals.prompt: Create a Go module (example.com/semver, stdlib only, Go 1.24). Package semver: Parse(s string) (Version, error) for strings like "1.2.3", "v1.2.3" and "1.2.3-rc.1", where Version is struct{ Major, Minor, Patch int; Pre []string }, plus Compare(a, b Version) int following semver precedence. Invalid input returns errors the caller can tell apart: empty input, a non-numeric part, and a leading zero. Write thorough tests.
evals.expected_output: Black-box package semver_test. No new dependencies: no go-cmp, no testify. No reflect.DeepEqual; Version contains a slice so it is not comparable with ==, so the test compares fields with == and Pre with slices.Equal (or a small helper that calls t.Helper and does the same). Success and error cases are separate tests: no wantErr bool or `if tt.wantErr` branch in a table. Errors are exported sentinels matched with errors.Is, never err.Error() strings. Failure messages read Func(in) = got, want want. Tables are slices of structs with a name field run through t.Run. A FuzzParse target exists with seeds and a property such as no panic or a round trip.

evals.prompt: Create a Go module (example.com/signup, stdlib only). Package internal/signup: a Service with Register(ctx, email string) error that rejects a malformed or already-registered email, saves the user through a UserStore interface (Get(ctx, email) (User, error), Save(ctx, User) error), and sends a welcome email through a Mailer interface (Send(ctx, to, subject, body string) error). If sending fails the user stays registered and Register returns an error wrapping the mailer's. Also a Notifier that, when Start(ctx) runs, drains a channel of registered emails in a goroutine and sends each a follow-up through the Mailer. Write the tests.
evals.expected_output: UserStore is doubled with a stateful in-memory fake (map plus the same not-found sentinel), not a mock asserting Get/Save were called; tests assert on stored state and returned errors. The Mailer is the one system boundary where a recording stub that captures sent messages is acceptable. The send-failure path uses a one-method stub that returns an error, not a failure flag on the fake, and is matched with errors.Is. No mocking library or generated mocks, no testify. The Notifier test has no time.Sleep: it waits on a channel, polls a condition with a deadline, or uses testing/synctest; t.Fatal is never called from a goroutine the test did not start on. Black-box package signup_test, helpers call t.Helper, and Service-level tests do not inspect unexported fields.

evals.prompt: In a Go service, an Order has a status (placed, shipped, delivered) read from a JSON API and from a database column. Show the type, how input is parsed, and a function branching on status.
evals.expected_output: One string-backed Status type with named constants, defined once. Zero value is unknown. A Parse function (also used by UnmarshalText and the DB scan) returns an error on an unknown value, never a silent default or bare cast. Per-value data comes from a lookup map, not a long switch. The branching switch has a case for every constant and no default.

evals.prompt: In a Go service with a store package over a SQL database, add Store.Rename(ctx, id, newName) that reads the current name, rejects a rename to the same name, writes the new one inside a transaction, and maps a unique violation on the name to a domain error. The nickname column is nullable. Show the store code and how you would test it.
evals.expected_output: The read and the write share one transaction via an inTx-style helper that rolls back on every non-commit path with context.WithoutCancel and wraps the commit error once. The unique violation is matched by constraint name and returned as an exported domain error; no driver or generated type, no-rows error or transaction handle appears in an exported signature. The nullable nickname is Option[T] in the domain type, never read without checking Valid. No time.Now() in the store. Tests run against real Postgres (one shared server per test binary, a migrated template database cloned per test, an env var to use an existing server) with no mocked driver and no TRUNCATE between tests.
